<!-- Source page: Nix Community -->

This article provides an overview of the Nix Community, to give an idea of who we — the users and maintainers of the Nix Ecosystem — are. To find the various ways to reach us, see <a href="Get_In_Touch" class="wikilink" title="get in touch">get in touch</a>.

## People

Nix Ecosystem users and contributors are a mixed bunch, ranging from hobbyist to professional, from industry to academia. Typical user groups include:

- **desktop users** using Nix and NixOS to make life on their personal machines easier;
- **power users** duplicating their environment across their personal and work machines;
- **gamers** using NixOS to declaratively configure unbreakable and sharable gaming setups;
- **developers** using Nix to reproducibly build their software, and to manage various development environments;
- **system administrators** declaratively configuring servers and clusters with NixOS and NixOps;
- **researchers** interested in making the computation in their research reproducible.

## Institutions

### NixOS Foundation

The [NixOS Foundation](https://nixos.org/community/teams/foundation-board) is responsible for providing operational and organizational support to the <a href="Nix_Ecosystem" class="wikilink" title="Nix Ecosystem">Nix Ecosystem</a> and community. It also funds the [official Hydra instance](https://hydra.nixos.org/) which builds the Nixpkgs collection.

The ecosystem is developed and maintained by many individuals and self-organised [community teams](https://nixos.org/community/#governance-teams).

### Consultants

Many companies utilize Nix-based systems for various purposes. Prominent examples include:

- [Mozilla](https://skillsmatter.com/skillscasts/9473-london-nixos-january-meetup) (see also [nixpkgs-mozilla](https://github.com/mozilla/nixpkgs-mozilla))
- [Tumblr](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6VH945-AaRY)
- [Shopify](https://shopify.engineering/shipit-presents-how-shopify-uses-nix) also [youtube playlist](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLRGI9KQ3_HP_OFRG6R-p4iFgMSK1t5BHs) by @burke
- [LumiGuide](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=J4DgATIjx9E)
- [RhodeCode](https://rhodecode.com/)
- [Awake Security](https://awakesecurity.com/)
- [Atlassian](https://www.atlassian.com/)
- [Replit](https://www.replit.com/)
- [Magnetic Insight](https://www.magneticinsight.com), a medical imaging company.

### Academia

Nix has its roots in academia; Nix was the result of [Eelco Dolstra's PhD thesis](https://nixos.org/~eelco/pubs/phd-thesis.pdf) in the University of Utrecht, and Hydra was developed at the Technical University of Delft. Some academic research continues to develop the Nix Ecosystem further - notably some work is planned on [incremental builds](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AED-dgCa9GU) by Guillaume Maudoux as part of his PhD.

Nix is also being extensively used to manage powerful computing clusters, since its resolution of dependency problems allows letting users install packages ad-hoc with greatly reduced risk of breaking things. Academic clusters utilizing Nix-based software include some of the biggest clusters in the world:

- [Human Brain Project](https://www.humanbrainproject.eu/en/)
- [Blue Brain Project](https://bluebrain.epfl.ch/)
